Rime dragons are the embodiment of the frigid cold and ice. These hardy creatures have adapted to harsh arctic climates, able to survive indefinitely in sub-zero temperatures. Rime dragons are shades of white and pale blue that perfectly camouflage them in their natural habitat, resembling glaciers or mounds of snow when curled up. They can break through large slabs of ice and dive into frozen waters in search of prey. Due to their natural lower body temperature, they can slow their digestive tract, which allows them to live a long time on little food. Large prey—such as whales, caribou, or moose—offer the best sustenance, but they aren't picky when it's time to eat. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Adult Rime Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4159) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 152 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet, snow vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=162) **Skills** [Architecture Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +20, [Arctic Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +20, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +22, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +13, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +19, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +18, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +21 **Str** +6 **Dex** +3 **Con** +7 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +3 **Arctic Hunter** A rime dragon's natural camouflage allows them to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) in arctic terrain without cover. A rime dragon also [ignores difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) from ice and snow and doesn't risk falling when crossing ice.
**Snow Vision** Snow doesn't impair the rime dragon's vision; they ignore [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from snowfall. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +16 **Will** +19 +2 status to all saves vs. [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) **HP** 175 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 10 **Radiate Cold** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) 10 feet. The adult rime dragon's presence lowers the temperature around them. A creature who enters or begins their turn in the aura must attempt a DC 26 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature begins to shiver as the biting cold affects it. It takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature's body temperature begins to drop. It takes a –10-foot status penalty to their Speeds and is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 until the end of its next turn.
**Critical Failure** Ice begins to form on the creature. They can't use Blizzard Breath again for 1d4 rounds. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Blizzard Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Piercing Ice** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Requirements** The dragon has [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) from Rime Shield; **Effect** The dragon launches the collected ice shards from its scales in a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), dealing 4d6 piercing damage and 3d6 cold damage (DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). The dragon then loses the AC bonus and temporary Hit Points from Rime Shield. **Rime Shield** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Requirements** The rime dragon's last action was to [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) at least 40 feet; **Effect** Water vapor collected on the dragon's scales quickly freezes over. The dragon gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and 10 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last until the end of the dragon's next turn.

item: 3 common runes of 9th level or lower etched upon their scales
fields.markdown:
Rune dragons have an innate insight on the power of runes. Most rune dragons keep a variety of runes etched on their scales, which their bodies can magically empower. They typically don't cast spells themselves, instead relying on their ability to create runes on the fly to produce desired effects. A rune dragon often refers to their hoard as their library, as it's full of important historical texts, plays, speeches, textbooks, and spellbooks written by people of different cultures in a variety of languages. While they can often speak a language with the aid of magic, they much prefer to learn languages in the context of their speakers so they can grasp the nuances hidden within the syntax and the magic within their symbols. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Adult Rune Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4364) **Source** [Monster Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=276) pg. 132 **Perception** +27; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), magic sense (imprecise) 60 feet, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156); seven additional common languages **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +29, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +27, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +25, [Linguistics Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +27, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +27, [Rune Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +29, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +25, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +25 **Str** +6 **Dex** +6 **Con** +7 **Int** +8 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +4 **Magic Sense** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) The rune dragon is aware of any active magical abilities and effects within the listed range. When the dragon [Seeks](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301), it gains the benefits of a 4th-rank [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) spell within the listed range (in addition to the normal benefits of Seeking).
**Runic Scales** The rune dragon's scales function as [_runestones_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3003). The rune dragon can't use the effects or abilities of the runes etched on its scales, but they can transfer these runes to appropriate objects. Transferring a rune to or from an item in this way requires 1 minute, during which the dragon is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58). The process is automatic and doesn't require a check, but if the dragon stops or is interrupted in this process, the rune is destroyed. A rune dragon can have any number of runes etched on its scales, though they typically have only a handful of runes etched on their scales at a time. **Items** [3 common runes of 9th level or lower etched upon their scales](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1770) --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +23 **Will** +27 +2 status to all saves vs. [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) **HP** 255 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), Shifting Runes, [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Canceling Rune** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** The dragon is the target of a spell that requires a saving throw; **Effect** The dragon attempts to unmake the spell's foundational runes. They attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell (counteract rank 7th, counteract modifier +26). If successful, the dragon is unaffected by the spell; other subjects are affected by the spell normally. The dragon can't use Canceling Rune again for 1d4 rounds.

fields.text: Adult Rune Dragon Rune dragons have an innate insight on the power of runes. Most rune dragons keep a variety of runes etched on their scales, which their bodies can magically empower. They typically don't cast spells themselves, instead relying on their ability to create runes on the fly to produce desired effects. A rune dragon often refers to their hoard as their library, as it's full of important historical texts, plays, speeches, textbooks, and spellbooks written by people of different cultures in a variety of languages. While they can often speak a language with the aid of magic, they much prefer to learn languages in the context of their speakers so they can grasp the nuances hidden within the syntax and the magic within their symbols. When the dragon Seeks, it gains the benefits of a 4th-rank detect magic spell within the listed range (in addition to the normal benefits of Seeking). Runic Scales The rune dragon's scales function as runestones . The rune dragon can't use the effects or abilities of the runes etched on its scales, but they can transfer these runes to appropriate objects. Transferring a rune to or from an item in this way requires 1 minute, during which the dragon is off-guard. The process is automatic and doesn't require a check, but if the dragon stops or is interrupted in this process, the rune is destroyed. Members Adult Rune Dragon (Creature 14), Ancient Rune Dragon (Creature 19), Rune Archdragon (Creature 23), Young Rune Dragon (Creature 10) Group Families Dragon, Adamantine, Dragon, Barrage, Dragon, Bog, Dragon, Brine, Dragon, Cinder, Dragon, Cloud, Dragon, Conspirator, Dragon, Coral, Dragon, Crystal, Dragon, Delight, Dragon, Despair, Dragon, Diabolic, Dragon, Empyreal, Dragon, Executor, Dragon, Forest, Dragon, Fortune, Dragon, Horned, Dragon, Magma, Dragon, Mirage, Dragon, Mocking, Dragon, Oath, Dragon, Omen, Dragon, Phase, Dragon, Requiem, Dragon, Resurrection, Dragon, Rime, Dragon, Rune, Dragon, Sage, Dragon, Sea, Dragon, Sky, Dragon, Sovereign, Dragon, Stormcrown, Dragon, Time, Dragon, Umbral, Dragon, Underworld, Dragon, Vizier, Dragon, Vorpal, Dragon, Wailing, Dragon, Whisper, Dragon, Wish, Dragonet, Wyrmwraith Alternate Abilities Many rune dragons find alternative ways to utilize their mastery of runes. Any one of the following abilities can be mastered by rune dragons. Remove Entangling Rune and replace it with one of the following. ### Adult Rune Dragon: Runic Jail Single Action (arcane) The rune dragon conjures a prison that promises pain to those within and those who try to escape. The dragon creates a runic jail in a 10-foot burst up to 60 feet away. The area is difficult terrain and creatures outside the jail become concealed to creatures within it. If a creature uses a move action to leave the runic jail, they gain a detonating rune. The runic jail lasts for 1 round, but a creature adjacent to the jail, but not within it, can use an Interact action to remove the rune early. Whenever a creature takes damage from a detonating rune while within the area, all other creatures in the area take the damage of the detonating rune (basic Reflex save DC 34). The Catalyzing Rune lasts for 1 minute but can be removed if creatures adjacent to the rune spend two Interact actions. ### Ancient Rune Dragon: Runic Jail Single Action (arcane) As adult rune dragon, but the area is a 20-foot burst. Catalyzing Rune Single Action (arcane) As adult rune dragon, but the area is a 40-foot burst and the DC is 41. ### Rune Archdragon: Runic Jail Single Action (arcane) As adult rune dragon, but the area is a 30-foot burst. Catalyzing Rune Single Action (arcane) As adult rune dragon, but the area is a 60-foot burst and the DC is 46. Runedragon Spellcasters If a spell the rune dragon casts would deal energy damage, it instead deals the damage type associated with its Shifting Runes. Additionally, rune dragon spellcasters know the rune trap ritual and can fulfill the role of the secondary caster themselves. She ensures that rumors of her vastly supplied library are well known, but the exact location is not. Those who seek her knowledge can access the library for a time, depending on their donation, and anyone foolish enough to steal from her rarely lives to tell the tale. A shining, rune-inscribed scale is all that most people, even adventurers, see of a sage dragon during their lifetimes. Even then, only those familiar with dragon lore will likely recognize the scale as anything other than an elaborate spell scroll. Collectors and scholars of esoteric lore, sage dragons become increasingly reclusive as they age, and, even in their youths, they're prone to work through trusted intermediaries. For those able to locate and gain the trust of such a creature, even the youngest sage dragons are fonts of difficult-to-find knowledge and rare magical techniques. The oldest sage dragons are living combinations of gargantuan libraries and endless grimoires, accumulating the secrets of the Universe, and beyond, in their isolated lairs. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Adult Sage Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4163) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 156 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +20, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +22, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +22, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +27, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +22, [Scribing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +24 **Str** +6 **Dex** +5 **Con** +3 **Int** +8 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +24 **Will** +26 +2 status to all saves vs. spells **HP** 230 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) Eldritch Interference ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) 90 feet, DC 30. Overlapping fields near the dragon make spellcasting unpredictable. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the area must attempt a Will save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's eldritch interference for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** For 1 round, when the creature [Casts a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144) that either deals damage or restores Hit Points, they gain a status bonus to the spell's damage or healing equal to the spell's rank.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** For 1 round, when the creature Casts a Spell that either deals damage or restores Hit Points, they take a status penalty to the spell's damage or healing equal to the spell's rank.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the effect lasts 1 minute.
**Divert Essence** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** A creature within 90 feet [Casts a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144) that targets the dragon; **Effect** The sage dragon steals energy from the spell to protect itself, gaining [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to damage from spells equal to the triggering spell's rank until the beginning of their next turn. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 60 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+12 piercing plus sanguine knowledge **Melee** claw +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)), **Damage** 3d8+12 slashing **Melee** tail +25 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d12+12 bludgeoning **Ranged** thoughtbarb +25 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [range 90 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+6 mental **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646) - **7th** [Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493), [Energy Aegis](/Spells.aspx?ID=1512), [Synaptic Pulse](/Spells.aspx?ID=1710) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Overwhelming Proclamation whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Mystic Facility** The dragon can activate scrolls and wands of any tradition as if the spells they contain were occult spells. **Overwhelming Proclamation** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) The dragon exclaims hidden truths that only they have been able to understand, dealing 14d6 mental damage in a 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save). On a critical failure, creatures are also [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1. The dragon can't use Overwhelming Proclamation again for 1d4 rounds. **Reveal Shame** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Requirements** The dragon has successfully [Recalled Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about an enemy within 90 feet; **Effect** The dragon utters an embarrassing secret about the creature, unnerving them and their allies. Every enemy within 90 feet that can hear the secret must attempt a DC 33 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.
**Failure** The creature is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) for 1 round and frightened 3. **Sanguine Knowledge** The first time each encounter a dragon hits and deals damage to a creature with their jaws Strike, they receive information about the creature as if the dragon had succeeded at a check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about that creature.

Sea dragons' affinity with water grants them mastery over rain, storms, and floods. Those whose livelihoods are at the mercy of the weather and waves frequently venerate these great aquatic creatures. Most sea dragons respond kindly to requests, but, like the sea, they can be unpredictable and fickle. Sea dragons have disk-shaped scales like fish and webbed claws as well as large back and tail fins to aid in swimming. They appear in vivid and vibrant colors, like aquatic wildlife. Underwater flora and fauna grow and thrive upon older sea dragons, and ancient sea dragons often have a head of coral around their antlers, giving them the image of being crowned royalty. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Adult Sea Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1126) **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 78 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [wavesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=41) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Aquan](/Languages.aspx?ID=14), [Auran](/Languages.aspx?ID=15), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +23, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +18, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +26, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +19, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +22, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +18, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +21, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +20 **Str** +6 **Dex** +5 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 33 fed by metal **Fort** +22 **Ref** +25 **Will** +20 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 225 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Countered by Earth** If the sea dragon is targeted with an [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) spell or [_flesh to stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=123), they lose Liquefy until the end of their next turn.
**Fed by Metal** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) When a sea dragon is struck by a weapon made primarily of metal or affected by a spell that uses metal, many of the dragon's scales transform to mimic the metal. This grants the dragon a +1 item bonus to AC until the start of their next turn.
**[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17)** (aura, emotion, fear, mental) 90 feet, DC 30

Imperial sea dragons are associated with elemental water and oversee rain, storms, rivers, and oceans. They live adjacent to the civilizations of Tian Xia, ready to aid mortal affairs and prove their worth. For some sea dragons, providing assistance in matters of the weather and arcane knowledge is a duty. For others, it's a perk that leads to valuable tributes or delicious meals. Visiting petitioners are all too eager to provide, for it's said that when a sea dragon is pleased, the rain is gentle and plentiful. Silver dragons are among the most chivalrous of all dragonkind; they wield frost and cold as weapons, can walk on clouds, and dwell high upon snowy mountain peaks or deep in steep, misty valleys. Although they typically make their lairs among the highlands, the pursuit of justice leads silver dragons to travel far and wide—often into the very heart of realms overrun by evil. These exemplars of righteousness are ceaseless in their determination to help the weak, spread honor, and stamp out evil. Silver dragons are sleek and sinuous. Sky dragons live above the clouds near the summits of mountains. They maintain a strong religious tradition, a unique practice among imperial dragons that sets them apart as much as their wings do. Desperate souls risk steep cliffs and loose snow to seek these dragons' counsel, and most sky dragons gladly help those who make the journey, but they expel any express hostilities or badger without hesitation. The sky dragon's wings aren't true wings, but long fins fused to their forearms; their scales also form only very slowly. Young dragons coil tightly in their lairs as they absorb minerals that color and harden their scales. Even adults often wrap around pillars out of habit. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Adult Sky Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1129) **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 80 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Auran](/Languages.aspx?ID=15), [Celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Infernal](/Languages.aspx?ID=19), [Sylvan](/Languages.aspx?ID=10) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +26, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +21, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +23, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +26, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +21, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +21, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +19 **Str** +7 **Dex** +2 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 **Mist Vision** Fog and mist don't impair a sky dragon's vision; they ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from fog and mist. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +21 **Will** +26 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 235 **Immunities** electricity, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Countered by Fire** If the sky dragon takes fire damage, the elemental magic of metal within them is tempered. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and AC, and their jaws Strikes don't deal electricity damage. This limitation ends if the dragon uses Breath Weapon.
**Fed by Earth** ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) When a sky dragon is targeted by an [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) spell or effect, they leave a cloud of pulverized dust and gravel that swirls in the eddies of the dragon's flight. Any electricity damage it deals becomes good damage against fiends or positive damage against undead. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Breath Weapon whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **[Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=19)** 3d8+8 bludgeoning, DC 33 **Perfected Flight** A sky dragon can hover in place without spending an action, and they automatically succeed at all [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=30).

When the imperial dragons first arrived in [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), each was well-attuned to the elemental planes they hailed from. As the war between the [Elemental Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=8) raged on and the benevolent lords fell one by one, the [Planes of Metal](/Planes.aspx?ID=24) and [Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) sealed themselves away. For the dragons who originated from the Corroded Core, their very existence was now at stake. These dragons flew from mountaintop to mountaintop, seeking refuge from the then-perilous Tian Xia overrun by warring yaoguai. Finally, upon the mountain peaks of Chenlun, Gossamer, Kelsang, Kimu, Kullan, Kyojin, and the Wall of Heaven, celestial beings answered the dragons' cries for help. What the dragons no longer had in elemental [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505), these celestials provided through divine blessings and essence. With their nature changed, the dragons as a species survived. In time, their proximity to the sky and the deities they serve became their namesake. fields.text: Adult Sky Dragon When the imperial dragons first arrived in the Universe, each was well-attuned to the elemental planes they hailed from. As the war between the Elemental Lords raged on and the benevolent lords fell one by one, the Planes of Metal and Wood sealed themselves away. For the dragons who originated from the Corroded Core, their very existence was now at stake. These dragons flew from mountaintop to mountaintop, seeking refuge from the then-perilous Tian Xia overrun by warring yaoguai. Finally, upon the mountain peaks of Chenlun, Gossamer, Kelsang, Kimu, Kullan, Kyojin, and the Wall of Heaven, celestial beings answered the dragons' cries for help. What the dragons no longer had in elemental metal, these celestials provided through divine blessings and essence. With their nature changed, the dragons as a species survived. In time, their proximity to the sky and the deities they serve became their namesake. Their past as elemental metal dragons became but a faded memory and creation myth for all but the sky dragons themselves to remember. The most well-known of imperial dragons due to their deep involvement with mortals, the sovereign dragons' name comes from their mandate of selecting rulers—but at some point, the dragons themselves joined the list of worthy candidates. Other imperial dragons suspect the sovereign dragons offered their connection to the elemental cycle to attain forbidden magic, evidenced by their lack of any vulnerability to wood or ability to feed on fire, despite being creatures of the earth. Most hesitate to question the sovereigns' authority. While some appreciate their impartial nature, others fault this adherence to neutrality. Regardless, the sovereign dragons' charm and centuries of experience in subtle manipulation have made them exceptional negotiators. Almost all sovereign dragons appear gold in color. Their hair ranges from common colors found among humans to bright reds, greens, or blues. They're the only dragons with five digits per claw, a mark of special importance. fields.markdown:
There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Each enemy in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must succeed at a DC 36 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65). All these effects last until the end of the dragon's next turn. **[Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=65)** 3d10+8 bludgeoning, DC 36 **Inspire Envoy** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The dragon chooses a mortal and offers their august blessing in exchange for the creature carrying out a specific directive, such as defeating a tyrant or protecting a sacred site. The dragon can't use Sovereign's Rebuke again for 1d4 rounds.

Heralds of—and heralded by—the primal forces of thunder and lightning, stormcrown dragons meld the majesty of fierce storms and mighty dragons. Driven by emotion and curiosity, these mercurial dragons can change from friend to foe or threatening to thoughtful in mere moments. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Adult Stormcrown Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4179) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 172 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), motionsense (precise) 60 feet, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +30, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +24, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +24, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +22 **Str** +5 **Dex** +8 **Con** +4 **Int** +4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +3 Motionsense A stormcrown dragon can detect the movement of nearby creatures through vibration and air movement.This precise sense works only against creatures and objects that moved in the previous round. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +26 **Will** +20 +2 status to all saves vs. [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) **HP** 254 **Immunities** [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 15 **Weaknesses** [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585) 15 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 100 feet, DC 30
**Superconductor** **Trigger** The dragon is targeted by an attack or spell; **Effect** The dragon uses the displaced air or magical trajectory of the attack as a channel for its electrical energy. The dragon attempts a storm bolt Strike against the attacker, regardless of range. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 150 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+13 piercing **Melee** claw +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+13 slashing **Melee** tail +25 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=765)), **Damage** 2d10+13 bludgeoning plus 2d6 sonic **Melee** antler +21 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 2d6+13 piercing plus 2d12 electricity **Ranged** storm bolt +27 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d12+8 electricity **Primal Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Gale Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1994) - **3rd** [Wall of Wind](/Spells.aspx?ID=1753) (at will) - **6th** [Cursed Metamorphosis](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479) **Command Lightning** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Requirements** The dragon's last action was to use Draconic Frenzy or [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527) or [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) trait and they're in an area of stormy weather; **Effect** The dragon directs a bolt of lightning at a creature within 100 feet, dealing 3d12 electricity damage with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. **Coronal Cloak** When the dragon spends an action to Hover while in stormy weather, they become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) until they [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) or until the beginning of their next turn, whichever comes first. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges Galvanic Barrage whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Galvanic Barrage** ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) The dragon exhales a massive bolt of lightning at one creature within 100 feet, dealing 8d12 electricity damage with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. The lightning then arcs to a creature of the dragon's choice within 30 feet of the previous target with the same effect. The dragon can't target the same creature more than once, and they must have [line of effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=2382) to all targets. The bolt can continue to arc this way until the dragon runs out of targets or until a target critically succeeds at their save. The dragon can't use Galvanic Barrage again for 1d4 rounds. **Smooth Flying** The stormcrown dragon doesn't fall if they don't [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) during their turn, and they're unaffected by [strong winds](/Rules.aspx?ID=2821) or similar effects unless they choose to be.

Time dragons are implacable enemies of the sinister [hounds of Tindalos](/Monsters.aspx?ID=702), also denizens of the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=46). Although hounds of Tindalos also seek to prevent any tampering with the flow of time, time dragons relentlessly hunt down every hound they encounter, despite the apparent common ground between them. No dragon has told the reason for this enmity to outsiders, but scholars speculate that time dragons and hounds of Tindalos might have different, competing opinions for what the proper flow of time should look like. Occasionally, those stalked by the hounds are rescued by time dragons who appear from nowhere to slay their pursuers, although this isn't necessarily a lucky break if the intervening dragon also objects to their activities. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Adult Time Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4183) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 176 **Perception** +26; (28 initiative) [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=164), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=158), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +30, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +26, [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +25, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +28 **Str** +7 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +25 **Will** +27 **HP** 342 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) **Immortal** Time dragons age, but don't die from old age.
**Starflight** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) A time dragon can survive in outer space and fly at incredible speed, taking 3d20 hours to reach a destination within the same solar system or 3d20 days for destinations beyond. They can carry up to six passengers of at least one size category smaller than themself, protecting them from the void of space.
**Decelerating Dodge** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** The dragon is targeted with a ranged Strike or spell attack; **Effect** The dragon slows time to evade, gaining [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 150 feet **Melee** jaws +30 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+15 piercing **Melee** claw +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+15 slashing **Melee** tail +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+15 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 36 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=1482), [Time Sense](/Spells.aspx?ID=2611) - **3rd** [Behold the Weave](/Spells.aspx?ID=2601), [Time Pocket](/Spells.aspx?ID=2610) - **4th** [Morass of Ages](/Spells.aspx?ID=2603) - **5th** [Quicken Time](/Spells.aspx?ID=2604), [Stagnate Time](/Spells.aspx?ID=2605) - **6th** [Awaken Entropy](/Spells.aspx?ID=2600) - **7th** [Behold the Weave](/Spells.aspx?ID=2601) - **Constant (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** When the dragon scores a critical hit with a Strike, they recharge their Timeshift Breath. **Temporal Eddies** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The dragon [Strides](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to their Speed, leaving behind afterimages of their past and future selves in each space they move through. Until the end of the dragon's next turn, they can use any of these spaces as the origin of their Strikes, spells, and other abilities. Observers also perceive the dragon in all these spaces simultaneously and must succeed at a DC 15 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to target the dragon or fail to affect it. A creature can take a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) action to attempt to identify the dragon's true location with a successful DC 34 Will save. **Timeshift Breath** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) The dragon breathes a blast of temporal energy, warping time in a 60-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386). Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 36 Will save. The dragon can't use Timeshift Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is slowed 2 for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature shifts briefly forward in time, vanishing and reappearing at the beginning of the time dragon's next turn in the same location (or an adjacent space if their former location is occupied), unaware that any time has passed. While timeshifted, time pauses for that creature, and it cannot take actions or be affected by anything else.

Stories across Golarion warn children about the monsters that dwell in the shadows, but no story captures the reality of the umbral dragon. Natives of [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), these occult dragons are at home in the darkness, using it to their advantage both in and out of battle. Umbral dragons rarely worry about fighting fairly, emerging from hiding to strike unwary foes and using their magical breath without compunction. Similarly, in social situations, they often remain in the shadows, operating through other creatures. Even in direct conversation, they frequently obscure their true intent, preferring to avoid ever being pinned down with a solid answer. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Adult Umbral Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4187) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 180 **Perception** +26; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), voidsense (precise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=162), [Shadowtongue](/Languages.aspx?ID=166) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +26, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +29, [Netherworld Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +30 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +4 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +4 **Hide in Shadows** The dragon can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) in [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) even if they don't have [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372).
**Voidsense** The dragon can taste animating void energy, allowing them to sense creatures with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83) as a precise sense. It can also sense [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) creatures with void healing, like [shadows](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=469), when they are inside solid objects. --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +27 **Ref** +24 **Will** +27 +2 to all saves vs. [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) **HP** 275 **Immunities** [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) Umbral Pall ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) 120 feet. Shadows surround the dragon. The radius of all light from light sources and the areas of light spells in the aura are halved.
**Pin Shadow** ([shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) **Trigger** A creature within reach of the dragon's claw uses a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action or leaves a square during a move action it's using; **Requirements** The triggering creature is in [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) or [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) and has a shadow; **Effect** The dragon makes a claw Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, the trigger creature also has its shadow pinned in place, restricting its movement. The creature treats the area of the dragon's aura as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2586) until it uses an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to unpin its shadow. If the area was already difficult terrain, the creature treats it as greater difficult terrain. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** jaws +30 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)), **Damage** 3d8+16 piercing plus 1d8 void **Melee** claw +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d6+16 slashing **Melee** tail +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+16 bludgeoning **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646) - **7th** [Darkness](/Spells.aspx?ID=1480) (at will), [Umbral Journey](/Spells.aspx?ID=1729) **Devour Undead** The dragon's jaws Strikes have the benefit of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune and deal an additional 5d6 force damage to undead. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges its Tenebrous Breath whenever it scores a critical hit with a Strike. **Tenebrous Breath** The umbral dragon exhales in one of two ways. They can't use Tenebrous Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Darkness** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The dragon breathes a blast of darkness that deals 16d6 void damage in a 40-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures take force damage instead of void damage.
  • **Shadows** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) The dragon breathes a blast of shadows in a 40-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must attempt a DC 36 Fortitude save.
    **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
    **Success** The creature is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 2 for 1 round.
    **Failure** The creature is enfeebled 2 for 1 minute.
    **Critical Failure** The creature is enfeebled 2 for 1 minute and [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round.

While the other primal dragons hail from the Elemental Planes, the cruel and unceasingly malicious umbral dragons originate in the depths of the Shadow Plane. Their sleek black scales and serpentine grace allow them to strike from hiding, and they are known for playing with their prey before finally finishing it. These creatures of shadowy energy and unwholesome appetites prefer the necrotic flesh of undead creatures to any other meal. This strange hunger can be of accidental benefit to nearby humanoid societies, but ultimately they hunt and kill undead creatures for the taste, rather than out of any desire to protect others from the undead. The benefit is always short-lived, however. When umbral dragons exhaust their preferred prey, they turn on whatever living creatures happen to be nearby. Umbral dragons sometimes go to great lengths to obtain their favorite meals, even creating undead creatures that they then feast upon. For all their power, umbral dragons are uninterested in fair battles. When faced with foes that pose any kind of actual danger to them, umbral dragons flee into the shadows and seek to strike back through pawns or minions rather than risk their own lives. Their treasure hoards are varied and diverse, often augmented by loot stolen from crypts the dragons have turned into feeding grounds. Underworld dragons embody the pressure between tectonic plates, the heat behind geysers, and flash fires that ignite when the conditions are just right. Natural alchemists, they innately understand reagents and catalysts. While some research the effects of magic on material reactions, the majority of underworld dragons concentrate on building their hoards. They scour the world for carved gemstones and artifacts of precious minerals, both of which they see as distilled essence of earth's bounty. Underworld dragons appear angular and sharp; their scales glow as if superheated from within, and their hair flickers like tongues of flames. An intense fire glows behind their gazes, suggesting they could ignite items with a mere thought, and their breath ripples the air as a testament to the heat contained within their bodies. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Adult Underworld Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1135) **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 84 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) (imprecise) 60 feet, smoke vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +18, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +24, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +22, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +19, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +21, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +20, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +22, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +20 **Str** +7 **Dex** +3 **Con** +4 **Int** +5 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 **Smoke Vision** Smoke doesn't impair an underworld dragon's vision; they ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from smoke. --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +18 **Will** +22 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 195 **Immunities** fire, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Countered by Water** If the underworld dragon takes damage from a spell with the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait, the elemental magic of fire within them is momentarily dampened. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, their jaws Strikes don't deal fire damage, and also lose their sweltering heat aura. This limitation ends if the dragon uses Breath Weapon.
**Fed by Wood** When an underworld dragon is struck by a weapon made primarily of wood or affected by a spell with the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait, the dragon's internal fiery essences are stoked with the added fuel. Their breath weapon recharges, and the fire damage from the dragon's jaws increases by one die until the end of the dragon's next turn.

Underworld dragons make their homes close to fault lines, active or dormant volcanoes, and regions with natural seismic activities. Locations with hot springs and fume holes are particularly popular, as they provide many alchemical and magical ingredients. Aside from vaults stuffed with treasure, underworld dragon lairs are also laboratories, dedicated to uncovering secrets in cultivation, elements, magic, and any other mysteries of interest. fields.text: Adult Underworld Dragon Underworld dragons make their homes close to fault lines, active or dormant volcanoes, and regions with natural seismic activities. Locations with hot springs and fume holes are particularly popular, as they provide many alchemical and magical ingredients. Aside from vaults stuffed with treasure, underworld dragon lairs are also laboratories, dedicated to uncovering secrets in cultivation, elements, magic, and any other mysteries of interest. Several underworld dragon families have operated such labs for tens of thousands of years. Vizier dragons are primarily concerned with the education and cultivation of people. People fascinate vizier dragons in all their riotous, contradictory complexity. Why do some people excel, and others falter and fail? Why does one person become a saint and the next a tyrant? Why do some become legends in their own time, while others labor in ignominy? **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 34 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 [Adult Vizier Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4195) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 188 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=157), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=158), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +22, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +28, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +30, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) +27, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +29, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +26 **Str** +7 **Dex** +3 **Con** +5 **Int** +3 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +6 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +27 **Ref** +25 **Will** +29 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 300 **Immunities** dragontongue, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) **Dragontongue** When a dragon speaks, the universe listens. The dragon is immune to [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1674) and abilities that would prevent them from speaking if the source's level is lower than the dragon's or its rank is lower than half the dragon's level rounded up.
**[**Frightful Presence**](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 90 feet, DC 33
**Word of Wisdom** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** An ally within 60 feet fails a saving throw; **Effect** The ally improves its result by one degree of success, turning a failure into a success or a critical failure into a normal failure. The dragon can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds. --- **Speed** 50 feet, fly 180 feet, swim 50 feet **Melee** jaws +30 ([Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+15 piercing plus 3d6 fire **Melee** claw +30 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d6+15 slashing **Melee** tail +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+15 bludgeoning **Melee** horns +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 36 - **3rd** [Dream Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=1503) (×2), [Humanoid Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=1560) (at will) - **5th** [Dreaming Potential](/Spells.aspx?ID=1504) - **Constant (5th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one horns Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges Powerful Utterance whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Powerful Utterance** The dragon expresses their power in one of two ways. The dragon can't use Powerful Utterance again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Ardent Proclamation** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), fire) The dragon breathes a blast of flame in a 40-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) that deals 16d6 fire damage (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).
  • **Chastising Word** ([mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) The dragon chides the targets strictly enough to leave the mind reeling. Each creature within a 40-foot cone must succeed at a DC 36 Will save or become [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 2 for 1 minute (or stupefied 3 on a critical failure).
**Word of Advice** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The dragon is a skilled mentor, and commands its students like a general. An ally within 60 feet of the dragon can [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) once and [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) once, in any order. If it hits, the Strike deals an additional 3d6 fire damage. **Word of Caution** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Wise people listen when a vizier dragon speaks. An ally within 60 feet of the dragon gains [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to the vizier dragon's Powerful Utterance and [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 15 to all other damage for 1 round.

Vorpal dragons are most notorious for their keen [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) magic. Even the least of these dragons can sever a foe's head in a single lucky stroke. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite creature: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. These conditions are suppressed if the body holds its head, and don't apply to actions performed exclusively by the head, mind, or voice. If the body is killed, the head can live on, but destroying the head kills the body as well. This effect can be reversed by taking a 2-action activity, which has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait, to firmly reattach the severed head to the correct body. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite creature: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. Some might even wear their favorite severed heads as a macabre necklace. Canny, patient, and creative, wailing dragons are adepts of sound and psychology. With both their physiology and innate connection to arcane magic allowing them to produce and shape sound waves, these reclusive creatures are heard much more often than seen. Named for their tendency to use uncanny keening vocalizations to communicate across long distances and startle prey, wailing dragons haunt locations that create interesting or useful echoes, such as canyons or caverns. Though ruthless predators when needed, most wailing dragons devote their energy toward investigating the effects sound has on the environment and the bodies and minds of creatures. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Adult Wailing Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4203) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 196 **Perception** +22; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), echolocation (precise) 120 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +19, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +21, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +17, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +19, [Music Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +17, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +17, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +19 **Str** +7 **Dex** +5 **Con** +3 **Int** +0 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +5 **Echolocation** A wailing dragon can use its hearing as a precise sense at the listed range. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +19 **Ref** +22 **Will** +17 +2 status to all saves vs. [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) and [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) **HP** 215 **Immunities** [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 15 Subsonic Drone ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) 90 feet, A creature who enters or begins their turn in the area must attempt a DC 26 Fortitude save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's subsonic drone for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1.
**Failure** The creature is sickened 2.

Whisper dragons are keen collectors of rumors and secrets who spend centuries honing their information networks and relationships. They generally do so not out of an intent to hold the information over others or to use for their own machinations, but simply because the process of learning and gathering information is fulfilling. As a reaction when the affected creature attempts a check, the dragon can reveal their secret to discomfit them, requiring them to roll twice and take the lower result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

The most feral and least intelligent of all the chromatic dragons, white dragons are brutish, predatory, and chiefly motivated by self-preservation. Nearly all other dragons look down on white dragons as hopelessly hotheaded and dull, though this does not make them any less dangerous—in fact, it may mean the opposite. It’s nearly impossible to treat with white dragons, not because they lack the capacity to do so, but because they just don’t care to. They are as difficult to deal with as they are quick to anger, and they become incensed at almost anything. When a white dragon does speak, it spews threats, inane jokes, and incoherent babbling as a prelude to attacking—and when the attack comes, it’s bloody and relentless. Thankfully, white dragons prefer very cold, remote locations that are far from people. Dwelling on glacial mountaintops or in ice caverns beneath forbidding tundra, they treat the lands around them as their own personal hunting grounds. They fly out to feed or terrorize other creatures, especially those who trespass near the dragon’s territory, then bring any treasure back to be displayed in icy niches in their lairs. They collect all kinds of valuables, with a slight preference for items with high utility—such as tools, trade goods, and fine food—over coins or jewels. The ability to shape ice lets white dragons rearrange their lairs exactly to their specifications, and they take great pride in how they’ve decorated their homes over the years. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 27 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 22 [Adult White Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=140) **Source** [Bestiary](/Sources.aspx?ID=2) pg. 114 **Perception** +20; darkvision, scent (imprecise) 60 feet, snow vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +16, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +15, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +23, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +19, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +18 **Str** +7 **Dex** +2 **Con** +5 **Int** +1 **Wis** +2 **Cha** +1 **Snow Vision** Snow doesn’t impair a white dragon’s vision; it ignores concealment from snowfall. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +19 **Will** +17 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 215 **Immunities** cold, paralyzed, sleep **Weaknesses** fire 10 **Dragon Chill** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65)); 5 feet, 2d6 cold damage (DC 27 basic Reflex)
**Frightful Presence** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) 90 feet, DC 27
**Freezing Blood** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27)); **Trigger** An adjacent creature deals piercing or slashing damage to the dragon. **Effect** The dragon’s blood sprays on the creature, dealing 2d6 cold damage. A creature that takes cold damage in this way is slowed 1 for 1 round. --- **Speed** 30 feet, fly 120 feet; ice climb 30 feet **Melee** jaws +23 ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d10+13 piercing plus 2d6 cold **Melee** claw +23 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 2d8+13 slashing **Melee** tail +22 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+11 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 27 - **1st** [Gust of Wind](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) (at will) - **2nd** [Obscuring Mist](/Spells.aspx?ID=210) (at will) **Breath Weapon ** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65)) The dragon breathes a cloud of frost that deals 11d6 cold damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 29 basic Reflex save). It can't use Breath Weapon again for 1d4 rounds. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order **Draconic Momentum** When the dragon scores a critical hit with a Strike, it recharges its Breath Weapon. **Ground Slam** The dragon slams into the ground. It can do this if it's on the ground or Flying within 10 feet of the ground. Each creature on the ground within 10 feet must succeed at a DC 29 Reflex save or fall prone and take 3d6 bludgeoning damage. The dragon can then Step. **Ice Climb** A white dragon can climb on ice as though it had the listed climb Speed. It ignores difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain from ice and snow and doesn't risk falling when crossing ice. **Shape Ice** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157), [Water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) The dragon reshapes a cube of ice or snow it touches, up to 10 feet across. Any creature standing atop the ice must succeed at a DC 15 Reflex save or Acrobatic check. On a failure, the creature falls prone atop the ice; on a critical failure, it falls off the ice entirely and is also prone.
White Dragon Spellcasters White dragon spellcasters tend to cast the following spells. **Young White Dragon**
**Arcane Prepared Spells** DC 24, attack +16; **2nd** [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [_resist energy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=256); **1st** [_ray of enfeeblement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=244), [_true strike_ (×2)](/Spells.aspx?ID=345); **Cantrips (2nd)** [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [_ghost sound_](/Spells.aspx?ID=132), [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245), [_read aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=246) **Adult White Dragon**
**Arcane Prepared Spells** DC 29, attack +21; As young white dragon, plus **4th** [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69), [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128); **3rd** [_earthbind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=94), [_haste_](/Spells.aspx?ID=147), [_vampiric touch_](/Spells.aspx?ID=354); **Cantrips (4th)** [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [_ghost sound_](/Spells.aspx?ID=132), [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245), [_read aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=246)

Young White Dragon Arcane Prepared Spells DC 24, attack +16; 2nd dispel magic , invisibility , resist energy ; 1st ray of enfeeblement , true strike (×2); Cantrips (2nd) detect magic , ghost sound , mage hand , ray of frost , read aura Adult White Dragon Arcane Prepared Spells DC 29, attack +21; As young white dragon, plus 4th charm , dimension door , freedom of movement ; 3rd earthbind , haste , vampiric touch ; Cantrips (4th) detect magic , ghost sound , mage hand , ray of frost , read aura Creature Family Dragon, White Source Bestiary pg. 113 The most feral and least intelligent of all the chromatic dragons, white dragons are brutish, predatory, and chiefly motivated by self-preservation. Nearly all other dragons look down on white dragons as hopelessly hotheaded and dull, though this does not make them any less dangerous—in fact, it may mean the opposite. It's nearly impossible to treat with white dragons, not because they lack the capacity to do so, but because they just don't care to. They are as difficult to deal with as they are quick to anger, and they become incensed at almost anything. When a white dragon does speak, it spews threats, inane jokes, and incoherent babbling as a prelude to attacking—and when the attack comes, it's bloody and relentless. Thankfully, white dragons prefer very cold, remote locations that are far from people. Dwelling on glacial mountaintops or in ice caverns beneath forbidding tundra, they treat the lands around them as their own personal hunting grounds. They fly out to feed or terrorize other creatures, especially those who trespass near the dragon's territory, then bring any treasure back to be displayed in icy niches in their lairs. They collect all kinds of valuables, with a slight preference for items with high utility—such as tools, trade goods, and fine food—over coins or jewels. The ability to shape ice lets white dragons rearrange their lairs exactly to their specifications, and they take great pride in how they've decorated their homes over the years. Here are some examples of who might be scheming. The monarch's spouse or children The royal pet (a druid in disguise) The grand vizier Visiting ambassadors or nobles Palace champion Palace doctor Kitchen staff Court jester Know Your Social Events Ball : a formal dance party that often includes a banquet Banquet : an elaborate formal meal for a large number of people Debutante Ball : a ball where upper-class youths formally enter society as adults Gala : a social occasion with special entertainment or performances Hunt : a formal hunting competition among the nobility and royals of court Masque : a dramatic performance with singing, dancing, pantomime, and dialogue Social Warfare Though courtiers might have guards and servants at their command, their most potent forces are their connections outside of court and the will of the common people. fields.text: Advisor Trusted counselors of the court, advisors whisper words of guidance in the ears of those in power. Many nobles lean so heavily on their counsel that they make few decisions without them and insist on their attendance at all meetings and public events. Advisors are often master manipulators, and their guidance can shape a barony or even a kingdom—for good or ill. **Divine Innate Spells** DC 40, attack +32
- **Cantrips (9th)**
[Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598)
- **4th**

- **6th**
[Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554) (×3), [Zealous Conviction](/Spells.aspx?ID=1760)
- **8th**
[Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=1495), [Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1720)
- **9th**
[Dispel Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (×2)

**Rituals** DC 37

- **1st**
[Diabolic Pact](/Rituals.aspx?ID=143)

**Domain Spells** 3 Focus Points, DC 40, attack +32; **9th** see false divinity

**False Divinity**   The advodaza chooses two domains, typically chosen from the following list: [ambition](/Domains.aspx?ID=64), [darkness](/Domains.aspx?ID=69), [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76), [might](/Domains.aspx?ID=83), [trickery](/Domains.aspx?ID=94), [tyranny](/Domains.aspx?ID=96), [wealth](/Domains.aspx?ID=99), or [zeal](/Domains.aspx?ID=100). The advodaza gains both domains' initial domain spells as well as the advanced domain spell from one of the domains, all heightened to 9th rank.

**Infernal Mark** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The advodaza touches a willing creature and marks it with a glyph that functions as a 9th-rank [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1673), which the devil can make visible or invisible. The target gains 1 Focus Point if it didn’t already have any, and the advodaza grants it one of their initial domain spells as a focus spell. The marked creature and the advodaza can communicate telepathically with each other while on the same plane. The advodaza can maintain up to 10 Infernal Marks at a time; if they create another after reaching this limit, the oldest mark is Dismissed. The advodaza can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) any number of Infernal Marks with a single action.

**Punish Disciple** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The advodaza chooses up to three creatures bearing their Infernal Mark that are on the same plane as the advodaza, dealing 8d6 spirit damage to each creature (DC 40 basic Fortitude save).

</column>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_2_AdditionalLore.png">Apotheosis Aspirations</title>

The advodazas outside Hell often fill the vacancy left by a dead or missing god. They masquerade as the lost deity, tempting ex-priests with a new patron and ultimately corrupting their new cult. The more followers an advodaza commands, the more their divine power grows. Large cults might allow an advodaza to access an additional domain—or, in exceptional cases, even grant divine spells to worshippers. Hell's scholars have posited that especially powerful advodazas seek to perform a ritual that would sacrifice most of their cult and transform the devil into an [infernal duke](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=28).

</aside>

Creature Family Devil Source Monster Core pg. 86 Masters of corruption and architects of conquest, devils seek both to tempt mortal life to join in their pursuit of all things profane and to spread tyranny throughout all worlds. The temptations they offer mortals range from great powers granted by the signing of an infernal contract to twisted favors following a whispered pledge to a diabolic patron, or any number of even subtler exchanges. Those who succumb to these temptations find themselves consigned to an afterlife of endless torment in the pits of Hell, wherein the only hope of escape lies in the chance of being promoted to become a devil in the infernal ranks. Every devil has a specific role to play in the upkeep of the remorseless bureaucratic machine that is Hell, from soldiers and scholars to inquisitors, lawyers, judges, and executioners. Lowly orts perform subservient labor to more powerful and specialized devils, such as infantry and contract devils, while the greatest nessaris command entire infernal armies. Asmodeus stands at the apex of the structure he created, but the layers below him are marked by a constant jockeying for position. Most diabolic plans ultimately serve to improve the schemer's place in the hierarchy. Members Advodaza (Creature 18), Agadaz (Creature 4), Ayngavhaul (Creature 13), Bdellavritra (Creature 16), Cephalophix (Creature 5), Coarti (Creature 7), Deimavigga (Creature 17), Enfiron (Creature 14), Ferrugon (Creature 12), Gylou (Creature 14), Hellbound Attorney (Creature 4), Insidiator (Creature 1), Instillo (Creature 8), Kylix (Creature 4), Levaloch (Creature 7), Merztorlegon (Creature 19), Munagola (Creature 11), Nessari (Creature 20), Ochiastis (Creature 15), Odvolos (Creature 5), Ort (Creature 0), Phistophilus (Creature 10), Sarglagon (Creature 8), Velavi (Creature 2), Vinculatti (Creature 11), Vordine (Creature 5), Vordine Legion (Creature 10), Zebub (Creature 3) Archdevils Eight archdevils rule the eight upper layers of Hell, while the deepest layer is ruled by Asmodeus. Barbatos is the doorwarden of Hell's uppermost layer, while Dispater rules Hell's largest city. Mammon guards Hell's treasuries, and Belial designs new weapons for Hell's legions. Geryon is the oldest archdevil and keeper of many secrets, while Moloch leads Hell's armies. Baalzebul is a brooding archdevil who has fallen from Asmodeus's favor, while Mephistopheles was formed from the plane of Hell itself Diabolic Divinities Numerous unique and powerful devils hold positions of power in Hell. The most numerous of these are the infernal dukes, many of whom were promoted to this position from already impressive statures as nessaris. The supreme ruler of Hell itself is Asmodeus, the Prince of Darkness. Between these two tiers rule the eight archdevils. Diabolic Locations The nine layers of Hell are the planar home of all devils, and they much prefer its tyrannically ordered environs to anywhere else in the multiverse. Yet devils can be encountered anywhere mortals can be tempted by infernal bargains or to seek diabolic aid. On Golarion, the nation of Cheliax is particularly aligned with Hell. Its government is based upon Hell's organization, and the state church is that of Asmodeus. Fiendish Relations Devils view daemons' constant hunt for souls as a short-sighted waste of potential, and demons' selfish destruction of society and flesh as uncivilized and obnoxious, but they do not loathe their fiendish counterparts. Indeed, most devils are more than willing to take advantage of daemons and demons as they can to further their own machinations. Fire and Ice The classic depiction of Hell is of a burning wasteland of magma and volcanoes, a searing landscape rife with the screaming souls of the damned. Yet those who have visited Hell know the awful truth—for its torments do not cease at eternal burning. Some regions of Hell are perpetually frozen reaches of razor-sharp ice and flesh-scouring wind, while others are miasmic swamps filled with poison and disease. Hell does not limit its torturous toolbox merely to the fires for which it is so well known! Other Devils The devils presented on these pages are a small sampling of the torments Hell has to offer. Other devils, like the mechanical warmonger devils, the cherub-faced and fly-bodied accuser devils, and the executioner devils beholden to the Queens of Night are but a few examples of these widespread immortal creatures. The Hierarchy of Hell Hell is a harsh plane of law with little use for compassion or empathy. As such, it exists entirely within a strict hierarchy, and this order extends to its denizens. While different types of demons correspond to various sins and daemons are associated with modes of mortal death, the different types of devils exist solely to fulfill particular roles in the infernal machine. On occasion, a particular devil can transcend the role for which they were literally shaped, but this often transforms the devil physically into the type suitable for their new role.

Aeolaekas, also known as stone azatas, embody the joy of stone carved by artists' hands or natural forces. Stone is often thought to be steadfast and unchanging, but, when viewed on a grander scale over vast periods of time, it can transform into things as diverse as intricate crystals and fine powder. Aeolaekas are fascinated by the gradual changes found within stone, from sand to diamonds to fossils to towering mountains. As a result of their stone affinity, aeolaekas appear less capricious than other azatas—though this is mainly due to them acting on a different geological scale—and some have willingly forged lasting accords or agreements with mortals. Aeolaekas often visit the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=30), fighting against evil [earth elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=409), joining jabali festivals, or simply wandering the veins and tunnels of that realm as they bask in its stony wonders.
